vars.prTitle: feat(auth): split rate-limited logins from bad credentials in login metrics
vars.prBody: The API login endpoint records every invalid form as `login.attempt` with `instance=failure`, including attempts rejected by the form's IP/username rate limits. This tags those as `rate_limited` instead, so the failure metric reflects actual credential failures and we can alert on rate limiting separately.
vars.injectPatch:
diff --git a/src/sentry/api/endpoints/auth_login.py b/src/sentry/api/endpoints/auth_login.py
index 56fd968..fa8cbc7 100644
--- a/src/sentry/api/endpoints/auth_login.py
+++ b/src/sentry/api/endpoints/auth_login.py
@@ -54,7 +54,10 @@ class AuthLoginEndpoint(Endpoint, OrganizationMixin):
             return self.respond_with_error(errors)
 
         if not login_form.is_valid():
-            metrics.incr("login.attempt", instance="failure", skip_internal=True, sample_rate=1.0)
+            # Distinguish failures caused by the IP/username rate limits enforced by the
+            # form from plain bad credentials, so the two show up separately in metrics.
+            instance = "rate_limited" if login_form.is_rate_limited() else "failure"
+            metrics.incr("login.attempt", instance=instance, skip_internal=True, sample_rate=1.0)
             return self.respond_with_error(login_form.errors)
 
         user = login_form.get_user()
vars.goldenComments: [{"comment": "`AuthenticationForm.is_rate_limited()` (src/sentry/web/forms/accounts.py) is not a read-only predicate: `_is_ip_rate_limited` and `_is_user_rate_limited` call `ratelimiter.backend.is_limited(...)`, and the Redis limiter increments the counter on every check (`pipe.incr(redis_key)` in src/sentry/ratelimits/redis.py, \"the counter is incremented when the check is done\"). `form.clean()` already calls `is_rate_limited()` during `is_valid()`, so calling it again in the failure branch of AuthLoginEndpoint.post double-counts every failed login against both `auth:ip:<ip>` and `auth:username:<user>`, halving the effective `auth.ip-rate-limit`/`auth.user-rate-limit` and locking users and shared IPs out after half the configured attempts. Also, every non-limited failure now increments the counters even when clean() bailed out before its own check.", "severity": "High"}]
